reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Driver.sigmaPoisson -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: the sigma-algebra generated by the Poisson random measure up to time t (the N-part
of "the filtration generated by W, N and F_0", sec. 2): sigma(N((0,s] x A) : 0 <= s <= t,
A in E) (equivalently sigma(N(B) : B measurable subset of [0,t] x E)). Faithful Lean: the
supremum of the comap sigma-algebras of omega |-> N(omega)(B) (values in [0,oo], with the
Borel/discrete sigma-algebra on ENNReal or N∞) over the generating sets B in [0,t] x E (or
(0,s] x A, s <= t). Harmless: restricting the generators to A with nu(A) < oo (sigma-finiteness
of nu: N((0,s] x A) = sup_k N((0,s] x (A ∩ E_k)) is measurable for the smaller sigma-algebra);
using closed/half-open time intervals ([0,s] vs (0,s]: N({0} x E) = 0 a.s., absorbed by
augmentation, though not literally equal everywhere -- record if so). Not faithful: no time
truncation, or generators that see the future.

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Driver.sigmaPoisson (Driver/Joint.lean:31-33)

Reading (locked): I expected the time-t sigma-algebra sigma(N((0,s] x A) : s <= t), with
"no time truncation" flagged as not faithful.
Lean: sigmaPoisson N := sup over measurable B ⊆ R x E of comap (omega |-> N omega B) (Borel on
[0,oo]) = sigma(N(B) : B measurable), the sigma-algebra of the WHOLE random measure. Its role:
LevyDriver.indep (sigma(W) independent of sigma(N)), the paper's "independent Poisson random
measure". It is not used as a filtration (the time-t version is Poisson.naturalFiltration). For
that role the whole-measure sigma-algebra is the right notion. Counts are [0,oo]-valued (oo for
infinite-intensity sets, which is the correct value under infinite activity), with the Borel
sigma-algebra on [0,oo]. Using all measurable B rather than finite-intensity rectangles gives the
same sigma-algebra (monotone limits) and is the standard definition.
Verdict: faithful.
